text:
jess: heads up
We keep getting support tickets where customers see a 503 and think the model failed. we need a clearer contract for partial/degraded results vs actual infra errors. quick thoughts on approach?

mike: i'm in favor of adding a clear machine-readable outcome header instead of overloading 5xx. humans can still see a message but SDKs should get a typed enum.

kai: agreed. small nit: prefer using a documented HTTP semantic if possible (e.g., 207 Multi-Status for partial) so middleboxes are less surprised. but 207 has weird connotations. maybe avoid inventing new non-standard codes.

sarah: +1 to machine enum. i'd rather we stick to 200 for everything the pipeline handled, and surface outcome via headers and a short JSON "outcome" key. this keeps client libs simple.

olivia: UX suggestion: console route page should show a small timeline and an "outcome" badge with hover details: outcome, reason, % of traffic, first/last seen. also an expand to show sample payload when safe.

raj: concrete proposal: introduce header X-RW-Outcome: success|partial|degraded|failed|rate_limited and X-RW-Outcome-Reason: lower_model|fallback_timeout|quota|circuit_breaker (freeform for future reasons). also body-level field rw_outcome for services that prefer parsing JSON. telemetry tag: api.outcome.v2 with same canonical enums.

mike: i like that. i'd add X-RW-Retry: none|client|server as a companion header so SDKs know if they should automatically retry or surface to user.

kai: on retry semantics, prefer explicit: no auto-retries for partial/degraded by default. recommend client retry only if X-RW-Retry=client. server retries are internal only.

sarah: SDK mapping proposal: map success -> normal response. partial -> return 206-like wrapper object (not an actual 206) + emit a PartialOutcomeWarning event. degraded -> DegradedRouteWarning exception with .outcome metadata. failed/rate_limited -> keep existing 4xx/5xx mapping. include typed enums in exceptions.

olivia: console copy for badge: "Partial" -> "Some inputs returned lower-fidelity outputs (see reason)." "Degraded" -> "Traffic served on a lower-capacity model to maintain latency SLO." keep short. link to runbook.

jess: good. telemetry needs stable enum names (no hyphens). let's standardize on snake_case: success|partial|degraded|failed|rate_limited and reasons: lower_model|fallback_timeout|quota_exceeded|circuit_breaker. use api.outcome.v2 and outcome.reason.v1 tags.

raj: rollout plan: server emits headers + telemetry first behind feature flag per-tenant. then SDKs pick up mapping. console badge after SDKs are released. canary: 5% traffic day1, 25% day2, 100% day3 unless major errors.

mike: ensure we don't log full X-RW-Outcome-Reason for PII tenants. strip reason in logs for sensitive tenants; header ok on wire.

kai: runtime impl note: put header emission at edge layer so it's consistent across runtimes. body field can be injected later in the response pipeline for backcompat.

sarah: docs: include examples for Node + Python SDKs and show how to opt-out of degraded fallback by setting prefer_strict=true in request config. sample: ```js
// node pseudo-SDK
const res = await client.generate({prompt, prefer_strict: true});
if (res.headers['x-rw-outcome'] === 'partial') {
  // app decides to re-run or degrade UX
}
```

olivia: console analytics: show 24h and 7d rate for each outcome and top reasons. add a route-level toggle "suppress lower_model fallback" that prevents runtime from choosing cheaper variants (enterprise-only opt-in).

jess: retention: store raw per-request tags 30d for debugging, aggregated per-tenant metrics 365d for billing/SLAs. keep reason strings trimmed to canonical enum in telemetry; freeform details go to internal trace only.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: feature/outcome-headers -> staging (adds edge header emitter + telemetry tag) :rocket:

raj: i'll draft a short RFC and include enum table, SDK mapping, and console mocks. assign to eng-platform + eng-runtime.

mike: runbook action: add triage steps: 1) check api.outcome.v2 2) check outcome.reason.v1 3) if degraded -> check route policy/tenant toggle.

kai: test plan: unit test header presence, integration test with canary, and a smoke test that ensures we keep 429/500 semantics unchanged.

sarah: final check: do we all accept X-RW-Outcome + enums + X-RW-Retry + api.outcome.v2 telemetry?

all: +1

jess: OK will close this thread and watch the RFC. we'll post a short note to #prod-notices once SDKs are published.
